planting.note: Divide and transplant in early spring or early fall while the soil is cool so the clump can re-establish roots before summer heat or winter dormancy.

directions: This compact sport of Hosta 'Golden Tiara' carries heart-shaped green leaves edged in a crisp white to cream margin, giving it a brighter, cooler look than its gold-edged parent. It forms a tidy, low mound well suited to edging shaded borders or massing under trees. Keep soil evenly moist and provide dappled or morning-only sun, since the pale margin can scorch in strong afternoon light. Divide congested clumps in spring every three to four years to maintain vigor and leaf size.

planting.note: Set divisions out in early spring so the small rosettes have a full season to bulk up before their first winter.

directions: One of the older miniature gold-leaved hostas, this cultivar forms a small, dense clump of rounded, shiny chartreuse-to-gold leaves that brighten shaded rock gardens and container plantings. Its small stature makes it a good choice for edging paths or tucking between larger hosta clumps where a low accent is needed. Morning sun deepens the gold color without the leaf scorch that stronger afternoon exposure would cause. Water during dry spells, since small-leaved miniatures have shallower root systems and dry out faster than larger cultivars.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich soil and allow two to three seasons for the large clump to reach full size.

directions: This large hosta forms a mounded clump of thick, blue-green leaves with wide, irregular creamy-white to yellow margins that soften to cream as the season progresses. Its substantial size and bold variegation make it an effective focal point in a shaded bed rather than an edging plant. Give it consistent moisture and protection from midday sun to preserve the blue cast of the leaf centers. Established clumps are slow to need division, but can be split in early spring if the center begins to thin.
